open_points.subject: startup cleanup of unreferenced file fixtures
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... are removed; nothing else is.
open_points.question: Does “value bytes” include an unreferenced file-fixture blob published by a failed trial-case or capture call, or must such a fixture remain because rule 2 distinguishes “value bytes and file fixtures” and rule 4 says nothing else is removed?
options: Remove every unreferenced content-addressed blob, including file fixtures
Remove only unreferenced value-carriage bytes and retain unreferenced file fixtures
A failed call is prevented from publishing an unreferenced file fixture
open_points.default_guess: Remove every unreferenced content-addressed blob, including file fixtures.

open_points.subject: determining whether value bytes are named
open_points.question: Exactly which database references make a blob “named”: existence of its StoredValue record, a reference to that StoredValue from another durable record, any record containing its digest, or reachability from a specified set of root records?
options: A StoredValue record naming the digest is sufficient
Another durable model must reference the StoredValue
Any durable record containing the digest is sufficient
Use reachability from an explicitly defined set of roots
open_points.default_guess: Treat an existing StoredValue record naming the digest as sufficient.

open_points.subject: failure while removing unreferenced value bytes at startup
open_points.text: On start, ... value bytes no record names ... are removed
open_points.question: What happens when an unreferenced value-byte file cannot be removed: does startup fail, continue while ensuring the blob is never served, or continue and retry at a later start?
options: Continue, never serve it, and retry on a later start
open_points.default_guess: Continue, never serve it, and retry on a later start, matching failed spool-directory cleanup.

open_points.subject: failed-run spool retention versus the new retention claim
open_points.text: so only trial fixtures and named values outlive a run, K-10
open_points.question: Is this claim limited to the content-addressed value/fixture area, or does it override K-10 and A14, which require a failed run's spool files to outlive the run until release?
options: Limit the claim to the content-addressed area; failed-run spool retention remains
Apply it literally and remove failed-run spool files when the run ends
open_points.default_guess: Limit the claim to the content-addressed area; failed-run spool retention remains.
